name: bluewater-23-wedgwood
lines: In seventeen sixty five, a potter with a bad leg got an order from the Queen of England.
What he did next is why you've heard of the money back guarantee.
And free delivery. And catalogs. And buy one, get one free.
His name was Josiah Wedgwood. Historians call him a father of modern marketing.
Here's his story. And the five moves you can steal today.
Josiah is born into a family of potters. In a town full of potters.
As a boy he catches smallpox. It wrecks his knee. He can't work the wheel like the others.
So he does something the others don't. He experiments.
Test after test. New clays. New glazes. Until he has it.
A cream coloured pottery. Clean. Strong. Good enough for a palace, cheap enough for a kitchen.
He has one of the best products in the country. And that is not enough.
Because every potter says his is the best.
Then comes the order. Queen Charlotte wants a tea set.
Most potters would deliver it, take the money, and tell their friends.
Josiah asks the Queen for something better than money.
Permission. To call his pottery Queen's Ware.
And to call himself Potter to Her Majesty.
He puts it on every invoice. Every order. Every ad.
Now he doesn't say he's the best. The Queen does.
Move one. Let someone your customer already trusts say it for you.
Next problem. People can't want what they can't see.
So he opens a showroom in London. Not a shop. A show.
Whole tables laid out, the way they would look in your home.
When the Empress of Russia orders nine hundred and fifty two pieces, he puts them on display before he ships them.
London comes to look at a dinner set.
Move two. Show the work. Don't describe it.
But there's still a fear. Pottery breaks. And the buyer is far away.
So Josiah makes three promises almost nobody else will.
He pays the delivery.
If it arrives broken, he replaces it. Free.
And if you're not happy, you get your money back.
Every risk the customer had, he took for himself.
Move three. Take the risk off the customer. Put it in writing.
And he doesn't wait for customers to come to him.
He prints catalogs with pictures, and sends them out.
He sends salesmen on the road with samples.
He stays in front of people. So when they're ready, his is the name they know.
Move four. Don't wait to be found. Show up first.
And move five is the one under all the others.
He never really sold pottery. He sold certainty.
The Queen trusts it. You've seen it. It can't go wrong. And everybody knows the name.
That's all a customer wants from a contractor, too.
Someone they trust says you're good. They can see your work. They can't lose. And they know your name.
A potter worked that out in the seventeen hundreds. With a bad leg and a kiln.
Your business. Our marketing department. Bluewater Co.
